messages.subject: Autopkgtests blocking testing migration - arch:all depending on 64-bit-only arch:any
messages.subject_clean: Autopkgtests blocking testing migration - arch:all depending on 64-bit-only arch:any
messages.body_plain:
Autopkgtests fail (by design) if the test-Depends are not installable. 
arch:any packages only attempt the tests on architectures where the 
package under test exists, but arch:all packages do not have that 
notion, so attempt them on all debci architectures.

If an older version of the package is already in testing and fails on 
the same architectures, this is ignored as a non-regression failure. 
However, if the package is not currently in testing at all, then this 
blocks migration.

This probably affects these r-cran* packages (but r-cran-dbplyr [0] is 
the only one I've fully checked) and an unknown number of r-bioc-* packages:
r-cran-animation r-cran-benchmarkme r-cran-benchmarkmedata 
r-cran-broom.helpers r-cran-cards r-cran-cubelyr r-cran-dbplyr 
r-cran-dtplyr r-cran-elliptic r-cran-gargle r-cran-gh r-cran-grimport2 
r-cran-httptest2 r-cran-httr2 r-cran-labelled r-cran-lgr r-cran-lobstr 
r-cran-magick r-cran-markdown r-cran-modeldata r-cran-modelr 
r-cran-mumin r-cran-prroc r-cran-sjmisc r-cran-skimr r-cran-svglite 
r-cran-vdiffr r-cran-webfakes

A previous discussion [1] (of a non-R scientific package) recommended 
asking the release team to unblock such packages (i.e. ignore the 
autopkgtest failure).  If nobody objects, I intend to do this.  (Because 
this issue does not affect packages that are already in testing, this 
will *not* need to be repeated for every upload.)

Altenatively, we could add Architecture: !armhf !i386 !s390x to the 
autopkgtests (as an explicit list and not a test-Depends: 
architecture-is-64-bit etc, because the whole problem is that being 
uninstallable counts as a fail).  (Please do not use Architecture: amd64 
[2] unless the package really is amd64-only.)

I do not recommend Restriction: skip-not-installable [3] because it 
applies everywhere, i.e. will also completely skip the tests if some bug 
makes the package's test-Depends uninstallable everywhere; it is also 
deprecated.

[0] https://ci.debian.net/packages/r/r-cran-dbplyr/testing/i386/71199543/
[1] https://lists.debian.org/debian-release/2025/01/msg00020.html
[2] 
https://salsa.debian.org/r-pkg-team/r-cran-broom/-/commit/c1503cf577f1f20c97608909b8c55801ce8b8d75
[3] 
https://salsa.debian.org/ci-team/autopkgtest/-/blob/master/doc/README.package-tests.rst?ref_type=heads

architecture-is-little-endian would probably work.

uninstallability) on i386, but plausibly a mild one (rounding).

have that, and only one package of any sort (kanboard) does.)

r-cran-broom and r-cran-modelr have amd64-only tests to get around this;

Hi Dirk,

I have been monintoring your packages this month and took action to remove the
blocking issues from the arch-restriction, as well as the blocking issues from
the risc64 architecture.  Now the situation looks much better:

https://udd.debian.org/dmd/?edd at debian.org

 - The quantmod, ttr and tseries packages are going to migrate after xts in a
   couple of days.

 - car is blocked by pbkrtest because of reproducibility failues, where
   reproduce.debian.net attempts to rebuild the package in an environment
   similar to the one used when the package was uploaded.  In my impression,
   the simplest solution would be that you upload a Debian revision, which
   I expect reproduce.debian.net will be able to reproduce.

So I am confident to say that this week the transition that your packages went
through after the architecture-restriction of the other packages will be over.

Remains the riscv64 issues, which I am tracking here:

  https://wiki.debian.org/R/riscv64/DebianIssues

For the moment I have been transiently turning off autopkgtests on packages
where riscv64 is failing, but I think that we can not release them without at
least warning our users riscv64 users that they will face bugs in their
computations because of NAs being turned into NaNs.  I will write a separate
message about this.

> I am gettting rather tired of this. Maybe I should orphan all those packages
> and focus on r-base and the ones I also maintain upstream (i.e. Rcpp).

The architecture-restriction, which you did not ask for, was excruciating
indeed, but now it is over (at least on your side) and I hope that it will bear
fruits, by removing a bunch of 32-bit and big-endian failures, which were
causing trouble by sinking the time we need to keep up to date with new
upstream versions, and therefore causing transition delays in your packages
through their dependency chain.

I hope that you will continue to maintain your packages, but in any case, if
there are some reorganisations you would like to do by transferring some
packages to us or adopting some that are key in your dependency chain
(not asking to increase your workload, but exchanges can be made so that
they are a net win for you), please let me know.

Have a nice day,

Charles

messages.subject: Proposal: a new binary package, r-pkg-team-core-architecture
messages.subject_clean: Proposal: a new binary package, r-pkg-team-core-architecture
messages.body_plain:
[This is not a new transition, just a passive replacement]

Hello everyone!

I propose introducing a new binary package, r-pkg-team-core-architecture, in
the dh‑r source package. It will be built only on the currently released 64‑bit
little‑endian architectures (amd64, arm64, loong64, ppc64el, riscv64). The
existing architecture-is-64-bit and architecture-is-little-endian packages will
be updated to depend on r-pkg-team-core-architecture, and most r-cran-*
packages as well as all r-bioc-* packages will depend on it. This ensures that
new architectures are not automatically enabled for the full R package
ecosystem without prior coordinated evaluation.

Description: Architecture gatekeeper for R packages in Debian
 The r-pkg-team-core-architecture package defines the set of architectures
 officially supported by the Debian R Packaging Team. Most r-cran-* packages and
 all r-bioc-* packages depend on it, ensuring that the R ecosystem in Debian is
 enabled only on architectures that have undergone proper evaluation and
 testing.
 .
 The restriction exists because historically many porting issues were addressed
 by disabling regression tests, resulting in reduced quality, increased patch
 maintenance, and disruptions during routine updates. Exceptions exist for core
 service packages central to the R dependency graph or for packages maintained
 by teams with a strong record in software engineering (e.g., rlib).
 .
 We ask porters who wish to enable full R package distribution on a new
 architecture to first build and test the full R package set outside the main
 Debian archive, using a custom r-pkg-team-core-architecture package. They
 should aggregate the results, identify the main classes of failures, and
 coordinate with the wider R community and the Debian R packages team so that
 most issues can be resolved upstream before enabling distribution in Debian.
 .
 Main benefits:
 .
 o For users: ensures that any distributed r-cran-* or r-bioc-* package meets
   the same quality standards as on mainstream amd64 and arm64 architectures.
 .
 o For porters: provides control over when to invest effort in porting R
   packages, enabling better prioritisation.
 .
 o For the Debian R Packages Team: reduces patch burden and improves control
   over time spent on porting‑related issues.
 .
 o For the Release Team: reduces delays in testing migration and transitions,
   and increases the quality of the Stable release.
 .
 o For the R community: encourages organised, focused reporting of
   architecture‑specific issues.
 .
 o For the broader Linux ecosystem: prioritises upstream fixes, benefiting
   other distributions as well.

Have a nice day,

Charles

--

your last upload of pbkrtest.

The presence of apt-cache is not guaranteed in build environments although it
is installed in buildds.  So this makes the package "unreproductible" from the
transition tracker's point of view, because it was built with an old version of
dh-r that relies on the presence of apt-cache without explicitely depending on
it.

The old version relies on apt-cache without depending on it, the new version

r-cran-pbkrtest 0.5.5-1 was built with it.  It finds this information from the
r-cran-pbkrtest_0.5.5-1_amd64.buildinfo file that was uploaded together.

messages.body_plain:
Charles,

I am not sure I can support this. 

To me, the current fix of outlawing armhf i386 s390x still seems more like a
bandaid for a self-imposed wound (due to choices made by the debian-r team).

Before deciding to permanently limit a well-known open source project (that
just won a major prize [1] referred to as a 'Nobel for Statistics') without
consulting with upstream strikes me as hasty.

This is Debian, and our priority per our founding documents are our users.
Why would we permanently deprive users of entire architectures of a vibrant
open source project? Do we do this in other parts of the Debian Project?  I
could of course be behind the news but AFAIK Debian has not decided to 'bury'
these three architectures. (And doing it distro-wide would be a differen
story.)

Would you be able to demonstrate for R and, say, a handful of packages that
there is fundaemtal "brokenness"?  And if you were to find it at the R level,
would it not your normal "Good Open Source Citizen" responsibility to
document this at the upstream bug tracker?  For R, that is its bugzilla; for
packages often their GH repos. Can we not start there?  That would also be a
net benefit to the R Project which AFAIK has no access to armhf s390x and
likely also little to none for i386.

So I think a better move would be to start by limiting autopkgtests to amd64.
And if we get to an the same 'all green' that CRAN has (even though we
knowingly handicap ourselves by introducing variability in package versions
as we tend to update some, but not others) we could then expand to more
platforms.

I think our choice of 'mixing' package versions when CRAN is more or less
ensuring a buildable cohort 'at HEAD' at each point in time is still the more
likely issue. And not the choice of build architectures. So the proposal
seems to address a sympton and not the cause. Looking at actual failures
(preferably for current packages) on the suspected architectures may help us
shed light on the actual causes.

Dirk

[1] https://rousseeuwprize.org/2026

--

messages.subject: Bug#1140569: unblock: R packages (test-)installable on only some architectures
messages.subject_clean: Bug#1140569: unblock: R packages (test-)installable on only some architectures
messages.body_plain:
Package: release.debian.org
User: release.debian.org at packages.debian.org
Usertags: unblock
Severity: normal

Many r-cran-* packages are arch:all but (test-)depend on other packages 
that are only available on some architectures (usually, only the 64-bit 
little-endian ones).  Hence, autopkgtests on other architectures fail as 
uninstallable.

If an older version of the package is already in testing and fails on 
the same architectures, this is ignored as a non-regression failure. 
However, if the package is not currently in testing at all, then this 
blocks migration.  According to a previous discussion ( 
https://lists.debian.org/debian-release/2025/01/msg00020.html ), the 
preferred solution to this is to ask you to unblock them.

(Other possibilities would be to add Restriction: skip-not-installable 
or Architecture: !armhf !i386 !s390x to these autopkgtests, but the 
first would allow packages to go completely untested if their tests 
accidentally became uninstallable everywhere, while the second is 
another thing to change if the set of installable architectures changes.)

Hence, please allow these packages to migrate despite their i386 and/or 
s390x autopkgtest failures:

(arch:all)
r-cran-animation/2.8+dfsg-1
r-cran-benchmarkme/1.0.8-2

messages.body_plain:
This proposal makes the most-of-CRAN architecture restrictions *less* 
permanent than the existing system, not more.

The whole point is to make it easier to change the set of included 
architectures, by allowing this to be done by changing one package 
instead of hundreds.  (In particular, a downstream distributor who 
disagrees with the whole concept can disable it entirely by replacing 
this one package with one that exists on all architectures, then 
no-change rebuilding r-*.)

Also, exceptions remain allowed: in particular, if none of your packages 
currently use architecture-is-64-bits etc, then they would not need to 
use this either, so you would not need to do anything.
